title: Route experiments: guardrail evaluator (soft-stop) + notifications
author: Rafael Mendes
description: This adds the initial guardrail evaluation pipeline for route-level experiments. The evaluator computes guardrail status per {route_id, experiment_id, variant_id} from the existing experiment rollups and updates experiment status to DEGRADED when thresholds are breached. In this PR the system is intentionally soft-stop only: we do NOT stop routing traffic or mutate allocation automatically. Instead we (1) mark the experiment as DEGRADED with a reason payload suitable for Console, (2) emit audit + internal events, and (3) notify the owning team via Slack (and optionally email via notifier integration). Motivation: beta customers and internal teams need a consistent way to catch regressions quickly (p99 latency, error rate, cost/token) without relying on bespoke dashboards. This unblocks Console guardrail banners and the first-pass on-call playbooks without taking on the operational risk of automatic hard-stop. Follow-ups: optional hard-stop + kill switch (tracked separately), alert tuning, and quality-eval guardrails once eval scores are wired. Implementation overview: - Adds GuardrailEvaluator job in experiment-service that runs every 60s per shard, evaluating active experiments only. - Fetches aggregated metrics from analytics rollup tables (5m window by default; configurable to 1m/15m). - Compares metrics to guardrails in experiment config (per-variant thresholds; defaults applied when unspecified). - Updates experiment_status table with: status=HEALTHY|DEGRADED, last_evaluated_at, breached_guardrails list, and a stable incident_key for de-duping notifications. - Emits OTel span and a metric: route_experiments.guardrail_breaches_total{guardrail_type, route_id, experiment_id}. - Sends notifications via internal notifier service (Slack channel + message templates) with rate limiting + de-dupe (no more than once per incident_key per 30m). Guardrails included in this PR: latency_p99_ms, error_rate, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, throughput_drop_pct (relative to control when available; otherwise absolute threshold). Non-goals: - No automatic stop / rollback (soft-stop only). - No statistical significance or long-horizon analysis. - No customer-defined custom metrics. Safety/operability: - Feature-flagged: route_experiments.guardrails_evaluator_enabled (default OFF). - Writes are idempotent and bounded; evaluator skips when analytics rollups are stale beyond 10m. - Notification rate limiting is per {org_id, experiment_id, guardrail_type}. - Adds runbook links in Slack payload (will be wired into alerts in follow-up). Testing: unit tests for threshold evaluation, de-dupe, staleness handling, and control-vs-variant deltas; integration test against local analytics fixture tables; dogfooded in staging with synthetic latency injection. Screenshots: n/a (server-side only).

testing: Unit: yarn test services/experiment-service -- guardrail_* (added ~70 assertions). Integration: services/experiment-service/test/integration/guardrails_e2e.test.ts against local rollup fixtures (Docker compose analytics + pg). Manual (staging): enabled feature flag for one internal org, injected synthetic p99 latency via traffic-shaper, confirmed: (a) status flips to DEGRADED within ~2m, (b) Slack notification sent once, (c) no routing behavior changes.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag (default OFF). 2) Enable in staging for internal orgs only; monitor: evaluator runtime, DB write QPS, notification volume. 3) Enable for beta allowlist orgs in 1 region (us-east) with 5m evaluation window. 4) Expand to all beta regions once rollup freshness is consistently <2m. 5) GA: keep soft-stop default ON for orgs with Console experiments enabled; hard-stop remains opt-in in a later PR.

review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): "Soft-stop makes sense for beta. Two asks: (1) add explicit rollup staleness guard so we don't page/notify on stale data; (2) rate-limit notifications harder (30m seems OK but make it per experiment + guardrail)."

Rafael Mendes (author): "Added staleness check (skip evaluation if rollup_age > 10m; also sets status_reason=STALE_METRICS in status payload). Updated de-dupe key to include guardrail_type and org_id."
Logan Wright (Telemetry): "Please avoid tagging route_id on the guardrail_breaches_total metric unless it's normalized; otherwise cardinality risk. Can we tag route_template_id instead?"
Rafael Mendes (author): "Switched to route_id_normalized (template form) which matches ADR-048 attribution dimension. Left raw route path out of metrics; raw is only present in debug logs."
Jordan Lee (Policy Engine): "Do we have a consistent definition of error_rate here (request-level vs token-level)? Also, control-vs-variant comparison needs to handle missing control traffic."

Rafael Mendes (author): "Error rate is request-level (5xx + gateway timeouts) aligned with metrics taxonomy; documented in guardrail_types.ts. For throughput_drop/control deltas: we only compute relative deltas when control has >= N=200 requests in window; otherwise we fall back to absolute thresholds and mark comparison_mode=ABS."
Chloe Martin (Console backend): "Can we keep the degraded_reason schema stable for the results API? Please include a machine-readable code + a human string."
Rafael Mendes (author): "Done. degraded_reason now includes code (e.g., LATENCY_P99_BREACH) + message + observed_value + threshold_value + window + last_good_at."
Allison Grant (Observability): "Add a span attribute for incident_key + ensure evaluator duration is measurable."

Rafael Mendes (author): "Added span: experiment.guardrails.evaluate with attributes {experiment_id, window, incident_key, breached_count}. Also added histogram metric route_experiments.guardrail_evaluator_duration_ms."
Sean Gallagher (SRE) (follow-up): "Approve once docs/runbook link exists."
Rafael Mendes (author): "Added docs/runbooks/route-experiments/guardrails-soft-stop.md and referenced it in the Slack template."
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main; feature-flagged and disabled by default. No migrations executed automatically outside environments where experiment-service migrations are applied.
release_notes: Route-level experiments: guardrail evaluation pipeline (soft-stop) to detect latency/error/cost regressions and mark experiments as DEGRADED.
Adds Slack notifications with de-duplication and rollup-staleness protection (feature-flagged).
